patients.summary: Retired math teacher who joined in 2017 with hypertension, stable schizophrenia on quetiapine, knee osteoarthritis and BPH after TURP. Primary adrenal insufficiency diagnosed in 2020, recurrent BPH, amlodipine edema, senile purpura, a Spigelian hernia and orthostatic hypotension follow; after his last visit he has an ED visit for urinary retention with post-renal AKI.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Levine phoned about joining. Says his old doctor retired over the summer and a neighbor recommended us. 70 years old, Medicare plus a supplement. Explained the membership and that his insurance still covers labs and specialists. Booked a new-patient visit 9/12 at 9:30. Asked him to bring his pill bottles and to sign a release for his old office's records; release form mailed to his home address.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
70 yo retired high school math teacher, coming over after his longtime PCP retired. Brought his bottles in a shopping bag, which helped.

HTN: about ten years, on HCTZ 25 daily since the start. Doesn't check at home. No headaches, CP, SOB.

Schizophrenia: dx in his twenties, one hospitalization decades ago, none since. Stable on quetiapine 200 qhs from the community psychiatry clinic, sees them twice a year. Denies AH/VH today, organized and pleasant, a bit formal. He would like us not to change anything about that med, which is fine.

Knees: OA both knees per old records, aches with stairs and after long walks, manages without pills for now.

Prostate: TURP in February this year at an outside urology group after years of slow stream on medication. Says he voids "like a young man" since and stopped the urology pill afterward. Has not been back to them.

Aspirin 81 daily on his own for years, "for the heart." No hx MI, stroke or stents.

PMH as above. PSH: TURP 2017. Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, quetiapine 200 qhs, ASA 81. NKDA.
FH: father HTN and an enlarged prostate. Mother osteoporosis and macular degeneration. Sister with autoimmune thyroid disease. Paternal uncle type 1 diabetes.
SH: divorced, lives alone in an apartment, daughter lives ten minutes away and checks in. Smoked about a pack a day for 30 years, quit roughly 12 years ago. A drink or two a month. Walks most mornings.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. BP 138/82. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, NT, no masses. No edema. Knees with crepitus bilaterally, no effusion, full ROM. Skin unremarkable. Affect mildly flat, thought process linear.

A/P
1. HTN - ok on HCTZ. CMP.
2. Schizophrenia - stable, psychiatry manages. CMP, A1c and lipids yearly for quetiapine monitoring.
3. Knee OA - activity, consider acetaminophen if it worsens.
4. BPH s/p TURP - asymptomatic.
5. Former smoker, 30 pk-yr - qualifies for lung screening: LDCT ordered after shared decision talk. One-time aortic ultrasound ordered.
6. Health maintenance: Hep C ab, TSH, CBC today. Records request to old office for colonoscopy and vaccine history. Flu shot when it arrives.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hello Mr. Levine, all of your blood work from Tuesday came back fine: kidney function, electrolytes, blood count, sugar, cholesterol, thyroid. Hepatitis C screening is negative. Nothing to change. The scan scheduling office should be calling you about the lung CT and the aorta ultrasound.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. They called already. Both on November 8 at the imaging center. D. Levine

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine given L deltoid, lot recorded. No prior reactions. Waited 15 minutes, fine. VIS given.

documents.title: Records from former primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 41 pages by fax from his previous PCP's office (closed practice, records held by a custodian service). Highlights abstracted for the PCP:
- Screening colonoscopy April 2013, normal, no polyps; no repeat advised given age.
- Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine Jan 2013, conjugate pneumococcal vaccine Feb 2015, Tdap May 2014.
- TURP February 2017 at outside urology, operative note not included, only the referral letter.
- BP readings 130s-140s/80s on HCTZ over several years.
- Psychiatry letters, stable on quetiapine.
Scanned to chart.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old records reviewed. Colon screening done 2013, normal; at 70 with a clean scope no further screening planned. Pneumococcal series complete. Tdap good until 2024. Shingles vaccine not on file; will discuss in spring. Nothing new clinically.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose non-contrast CT of the chest for lung cancer screening. Baseline exam. The lungs are clear without nodules, consolidation or effusion. No emphysema. Airways patent. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

reports.text: Limited ultrasound of the abdominal aorta for aneurysm screening. The aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation and is of normal caliber throughout. No aneurysm. Iliac origins unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.title: Lung CT and aorta ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Both scans were normal. The lung CT shows no nodules, and we would repeat it once a year for now. The aorta is a normal size and doesn't need another look. Have a good week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check. Winter was quiet. Walking indoors at the mall when it's icy. Taking HCTZ every morning, no missed doses he can recall. Psychiatry visit in January went fine, no changes.
Knees about the same.
No urinary complaints.

BP as charted, a touch high today; home cuff not used. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P: HTN, borderline today, prior readings fine; recheck at the fall visit before changing anything. BMP for K and Na on the diuretic. Shingles vaccine: recommended the two-dose recombinant series; Part D covers it at the pharmacy, he will go this week. RTC fall for wellness visit.

documents.title: Pharmacy vaccine notification

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request from the pharmacy for hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg #90. Last BMP March normal, seen in March. Sent per protocol, 90 days with 1 refill.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First AWV with us.
Health risk assessment reviewed: independent in all ADLs and IADLs, drives, manages own pills with a weekly box. No falls in the past year. Hearing ok, wears readers. Lives alone, daughter nearby. Advance directive: has a health care proxy (daughter), copy requested.
Cognition: three-word recall 3/3, clock normal.
PHQ-2 0.
Meds reviewed, unchanged: HCTZ 25, quetiapine 200 qhs, ASA 81.

Exam: BP as charted. Weight steady. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema. Gait steady.

Plan: annual labs incl. metabolic monitoring for quetiapine. Second year LDCT ordered. Flu shot next visit with nurse. Shingles series done. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza vaccine, R deltoid. Tolerated. He asked about the lab letters from the wellness visit; reviewed with him that they were all normal per PCP note.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual low-dose screening CT, compared with November 2017. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Normal heart size. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your screening lung CT is clear again, same as last year. One more next fall.
